name: MORTUARY CHAMBER
desc: 2-Body Laboratory and Hospital Mortuary Cabinet engineered for highly reliable, low-temperature cadaver preservation. Features 2 independent SS304 body compartments driven by dedicated cooling systems for each chamber using CFC-free R-404A refrigerant.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Mortuary Chamber operates on a dual-compressor, direct-expansion vapor-compression refrigeration cycle using CFC-free R-404A refrigerant to maintain cadaver preservation temperatures between 2°C and 6°C. Each of the two independent SS304 stainless steel compartments is served by a dedicated refrigeration system, ensuring thermal isolation and preventing cross-contamination between stored bodies. A microprocessor-based PID controller with a digital LED display continuously monitors chamber temperature via precision sensors and modulates compressor cycling to hold the set point within tight tolerances. Motorized forced-air circulation achieves rapid thermal equilibrium and uniform cooling throughout the chamber, while 50–100 mm polyurethane foam (PUF) insulation minimizes thermal loss and reduces compressor duty cycles. The integrated data logger and temperature chart recorder provide continuous, auditable thermal records in compliance with hospital mortuary and forensic pathology standards. This chamber is used by forensic pathologists, mortuary technicians, and medical researchers for short- to medium-term preservation of human cadavers prior to autopsy, organ retrieval, or anatomical study. It supports B.Sc/M.Sc anatomy and forensic science students in cadaver-based dissection and decomposition studies, and PhD researchers investigating post-mortem tissue degradation, microbial succession, or embalming efficacy. The SS304 interior resists corrosion from bodily fluids, formalin vapors, and disinfectants such as sodium hypochlorite or quaternary ammonium compounds, while the moisture-proof internal lighting and audio-visual temperature alarms ensure safe operation and rapid response to thermal excursions. The chamber meets relevant ISO 13408 and ASTM F1980-style environmental control expectations for biological specimen storage, though specific mortuary standards may apply locally.
sop: Ensure the mortuary chamber is connected to a stable 220 V (±10%), 50 Hz, single-phase power supply through the provided voltage stabilizer, and verify that the chamber is level and all drainage channels are clear.
Switch ON the main power isolator and then turn ON the individual chamber power switch for the compartment to be used.
Press the 'SET' button once on the microprocessor-based PID controller to enter temperature set point mode.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust the target temperature to the required preservation value, typically between 2°C and 6°C (e.g., 4°C).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and exit set point mode; the digital LED display will now show the actual chamber temperature.
Allow the chamber to pre-cool and stabilize at the set temperature for at least 30–60 minutes before loading any cadaver; verify the analogue temperature gauge and digital display agree within ±1°C.
Prepare the cadaver according to institutional protocol, ensuring it is properly shrouded or bagged and placed on a telescopic carriage tray or loading trolley.
Open the selected chamber door using the independent secure key lock, slide the loaded tray smoothly into the chamber, close the door firmly, and lock it to prevent unauthorized access.
Record the chamber temperature, time, date, and cadaver identification in the logbook, and confirm that the integrated data logger and temperature chart recorder are actively recording.
Monitor the audio-visual temperature variation alarm system; if an alarm sounds, immediately check the display, verify door seals, and contact maintenance if the temperature deviates beyond 2–6°C.

For routine defrosting, switch OFF the chamber, remove all contents, allow ice to melt naturally, and ensure internal drainage channels direct water to a suitable collection vessel; never use sharp metal tools to scrape ice from SS304 surfaces.

SAFETY WARNING: Always wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) including gloves, gown, eye protection, and respiratory protection when handling cadavers or cleaning the chamber, as biological fluids may contain bloodborne pathogens (e.g., HBV, HIV, prions) and residual formalin or disinfectant vapors can be hazardous; never operate the chamber with damaged door seals or bypassed safety alarms.
